outcomes.text: Relate the sub-cellular structures of animal, plant and bacterial cells to their functions.
Describe how sperm, egg and ciliated epithelial cells are adapted to their functions.
Explain how better microscopes, including electron microscopes, improved our understanding of cell structures.
Use number, size and scale, with estimations, and say when to estimate.
Relate units milli, micro, nano and pico, and calculate in standard form.
Core practical: investigate specimens with microscopes, with magnification calculations and labelled drawings.
Explain enzyme action, including the active site and specificity.
Explain how enzymes denature when the active site changes shape.
Explain how temperature, substrate concentration and pH affect enzyme activity.
Core practical: investigate the effect of pH on enzyme activity.
Calculate rates for enzyme activity.
Explain enzymes as catalysts building and breaking down carbohydrates, proteins and lipids.
Core practical: use reagents to test for starch, reducing sugars, proteins and fats.
Explain how calorimetry measures the energy in food.

topics.title: Transport in and out of cells

outcomes.text: Explain transport in and out of cells by diffusion, osmosis and active transport.
Core practical: investigate osmosis in potatoes.
Calculate percentage gain and loss of mass in osmosis.
Describe mitosis within the cell cycle, including its stages and cytokinesis.
Describe the importance of mitosis in growth, repair and asexual reproduction.
Explain that mitosis gives two genetically identical diploid daughter cells.
Describe cancer as uncontrolled cell division from changed cells.
Describe growth in animals and plants by division, elongation and differentiation.
Explain why cell differentiation matters for specialised cells.
Use percentile charts to monitor growth.
Describe the function of embryonic stem cells, animal stem cells and plant meristems.
Discuss benefits and risks of stem cells in medicine.
Describe the functions of the cerebellum, cerebral hemispheres and medulla oblongata.
Explain how CT and PET scans help investigate brain function.
Explain limits of treating brain and nervous system damage, including spinal injuries and tumours.
Explain how receptors, sensory, relay and motor neurones and synapses transmit impulses.
Explain the reflex arc with sensory, relay and motor neurones.
Explain the eye as a receptor: cornea, lens, iris, rods and cones.
Describe eye defects: cataracts, long and short sight, colour blindness.
Explain how cataracts and long and short sight are corrected.
Explain advantages and disadvantages of asexual reproduction.
Explain advantages and disadvantages of sexual reproduction.
Explain meiosis producing four genetically different haploid gametes.
Describe DNA as a double helix of nucleotides with complementary base pairs.
Describe the genome and a gene.
Explain how DNA is extracted from fruit.
Explain how base order decides amino acid order and protein shape.
Describe transcription and translation, with RNA polymerase, mRNA, codons, tRNA and polypeptides.
Explain how variants in non-coding DNA alter protein quantity.
Explain how variants in coding DNA alter protein activity.
Describe Mendel's work and the difficulty of understanding inheritance before its mechanism.
Explain how alleles cause inherited differences.
Define chromosome, gene, allele, dominant, recessive, homozygous, heterozygous, genotype, phenotype, gamete, zygote.
Explain monohybrid inheritance with genetic diagrams, Punnett squares and pedigrees.
Describe sex determination at fertilisation with genetic diagrams.
Calculate outcomes of monohybrid crosses and pedigrees as probabilities, ratios and percentages.
Describe ABO blood group inheritance with codominance and multiple alleles.
Explain inheritance of sex-linked disorders.
State that most features come from many genes.
Describe genetic and environmental causes of variation.
State that populations show extensive genetic variation from mutation.
State that most mutations have no effect, some small, rarely large.
Discuss the Human Genome Project and its uses in medicine.

units.title: Topic 4 – Natural selection and genetic modification

outcomes.text: Describe Darwin and Wallace's work on natural selection and its impact on biology.
Explain Darwin's theory of natural selection.
Explain how resistant organisms such as antibiotic-resistant bacteria support the theory.
Describe fossil evidence for human evolution: Ardi, Lucy and Leakey's finds.
Describe stone tools as evidence of human evolution, and how they are dated.
Describe the pentadactyl limb as evidence for evolution.
Describe how genetic analysis suggested three domains rather than five kingdoms.
Explain selective breeding and its effects on food plants and domesticated animals.
Describe tissue culture and its uses in medical research and plant breeding.
Describe genetic engineering as modifying a genome to add desirable traits.
Describe the stages of genetic engineering: restriction enzymes, ligase, sticky ends, vectors.
Evaluate GM organisms, including Bt insect-resistant crops.
Evaluate agricultural solutions for growing populations: fertilisers and biological control.
Evaluate benefits, risks and ethics of genetic engineering and selective breeding.

units.title: Topic 5 – Health, disease and the development of medicines

outcomes.text: Define health as complete physical, mental and social well-being.
Distinguish communicable from non-communicable diseases.
Explain why one disease can raise susceptibility to others.
Describe pathogens: viruses, bacteria, fungi and protists.
Describe cholera, tuberculosis, ash dieback, malaria, HIV, stomach ulcers and Ebola.
Explain how these pathogens spread and how spread can be reduced.
Describe the virus lifecycle with lysogenic and lytic pathways.
Explain how Chlamydia and HIV spread and how to prevent it.
Describe plant physical defences: leaf cuticle and cell wall.
Describe plant chemical defences, some useful as human medicines.
Describe ways to detect and identify plant diseases in lab and field.
Describe human physical and chemical barriers: mucus, cilia, skin, lysozyme, hydrochloric acid.
Explain the specific immune response: antibodies, memory lymphocytes and the secondary response.
Explain the body's response to immunisation with an inactive pathogen.
Discuss advantages and disadvantages of immunisation and herd immunity.
Explain why antibiotics treat only bacterial infections.
Explain aseptic techniques for culturing microorganisms.
Core practical: investigate effects of antiseptics, antibiotics or plant extracts on microbial cultures.
Calculate cross-sectional areas of cultures and clear agar using pi r squared.
Describe stages in developing medicines: discovery, development, preclinical and clinical testing.
Describe producing monoclonal antibodies with lymphocytes and hybridoma cells.
Explain uses of monoclonal antibodies: pregnancy tests, diagnosis and treatment, versus drugs and radiotherapy.
Describe how several factors combine to cause non-communicable diseases.
Explain how exercise, diet, alcohol and smoking affect non-communicable disease, including BMI and waist-hip calculations.
Evaluate treatments for cardiovascular disease: medication, surgery and lifestyle change.

units.title: Topic 6 – Plant structures and their functions

outcomes.text: Describe photosynthetic organisms as main producers of food and biomass.
Describe photosynthesis as an endothermic reaction making glucose and oxygen.
Explain temperature, light intensity and carbon dioxide as limiting factors.
Explain how limiting factors interact.
Core practical: investigate light intensity and photosynthesis rate.
Explain the inverse square law linking light intensity and distance.
Explain how root hair cells absorb water and mineral ions.
Explain how xylem and phloem structure suits their functions.
Explain transpiration and the role of stomata.
Describe translocation of sucrose.
Explain how light, air movement and temperature affect water uptake.
Calculate transpiration rates.
Explain how leaf structure suits photosynthesis and gas exchange.
Explain plant adaptations to extreme environments: leaf size and shape, cuticle, stomata.
Explain how auxins control phototropism and gravitropism.
Describe commercial uses of auxins, gibberellins and ethene.

units.title: Topic 7 – Animal coordination, control and homeostasis

outcomes.text: Describe where hormones are made and how they reach target organs.
Explain adrenalin's fight-or-flight effects.
Explain how thyroxine controls metabolic rate by negative feedback.
Describe the menstrual cycle and the roles of oestrogen and progesterone.
Explain how oestrogen, progesterone, FSH and LH interact in the cycle.
Explain how hormonal contraception works.
Evaluate hormonal and barrier contraception.
Explain hormones in IVF and clomifene therapy.
Explain why a constant internal environment matters.
Explain thermoregulation and osmoregulation as homeostasis.
Explain thermoregulation through skin and hypothalamus.
Explain shivering, vasoconstriction and vasodilation.
Explain how insulin controls blood glucose.
Explain how glucagon regulates blood glucose.
Explain the cause and control of type 1 diabetes.
Explain the cause and control of type 2 diabetes.
Evaluate the link between body mass and type 2 diabetes using BMI and waist-hip ratio.
Describe the urinary system.
Explain how the nephron filters blood and forms urine.
Explain how ADH changes collecting duct permeability.
Describe kidney failure treatments: dialysis and transplant.
State that urea comes from breakdown of excess amino acids in the liver.

units.title: Topic 8 – Exchange and transport in animals

outcomes.text: Describe why organisms transport oxygen, carbon dioxide, water, food molecules, ions and urea.
Explain the need for exchange surfaces and transport systems, with surface area to volume ratios.
Explain how alveoli suit gas exchange.
Describe factors affecting diffusion rate.
Calculate diffusion rate using Fick's law.
Relate blood component structure to function.
Relate blood vessel structure to function.
Relate heart and circulatory system structure to function.
Calculate heart rate, stroke volume and cardiac output.
Describe cellular respiration as an exothermic reaction releasing energy.
Compare aerobic and anaerobic respiration.
Core practical: investigate the rate of respiration in living organisms.
Describe levels of organisation from organism to ecosystem.
Explain how abiotic and biotic factors affect communities.
Describe interdependence in a community.
Describe dependence between species, including parasitism and mutualism.
Core practical: investigate organisms and environment using quadrats and belt transects.
Estimate organism numbers in an area from fieldwork data.
Explain energy loss between trophic levels and its effects on food chains and biomass pyramids.
Calculate efficiency of energy transfer and biomass percentages.
Explain human impacts on biodiversity: fish farming, non-indigenous species, eutrophication.
Explain benefits of maintaining biodiversity, conservation and reforestation.
Describe biological factors affecting food security.
Describe how materials cycle through biotic and abiotic components.
Explain the carbon cycle and decomposers.
Explain the water cycle and potable water production, including desalination.
Explain nitrate availability: fertilisers, crop rotation and nitrogen-cycle bacteria.
Evaluate indicator species as evidence of pollution.
Explain how temperature, water and oxygen affect decomposition in food preservation.
Explain how temperature, water and oxygen affect decomposition in composting.
Calculate rate changes in decay of biological material.
